answer: Each submission is priced by how far it moves the posterior, not by how many keys signed it. Once an answer has been read, nine clones of it shift nothing, so marginal payment decays toward zero while the cost of running each identity stays ferrous and constant: proxies, custody, upkeep. A farm can therefore occupy every vertex of the graph and still earn like one member, because repetition is priced as noise. Only independent conclusions pull payment, and that is exactly what a Sybil operator cannot mass produce. The rule is basalt-hard and needs no committee discretion.
